sources.title: Models | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit. The exact aion-labs/aion-2.0 entry explicitly identifies a variant of DeepSeek V3.2 optimized for roleplay/storytelling and gives release date 2025-12-21. It supplies no Aion-specific parameter count and describes no pruning, distillation to a smaller network, expert expansion, new modalities or other structural change. This is explicit named-model lineage, not merely DeepSeek-family resemblance.

sources.title: Aion Labs public models API
sources.evidence: Fresh unauthenticated API read confirms exact ID aion-labs/aion-2.0, the named DeepSeek V3.2 variant description, date 2025-12-21, context_length 131072, max_completion_tokens 32768, reasoning true and tool_calls true. No total/active count or structural-change disclosure appears. The architecture object describes text->text modality only; it is not the evidence for inferred MoE architecture.

sources.title: API Reference | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Defines per-model reasoning and tool_calls flags. Aion 2.0 supports reasoning_effort none, low, medium, high and max, with medium default. Explains that model created timestamps encode release dates.

sources.title: Aion Labs official Hugging Face organization
sources.evidence: Reopened official organization, which links aionlabs.ai and aionlabsai on GitHub. It still lists only Aion-RP-Llama-3.1-8B and its GGUF variant. No Aion 2.0 model card, configuration or weights are exposed here; that lack does not invalidate a labeled nominal inference from the developer-named base.

sources.title: Terms of Service of the Aion Labs API
sources.evidence: Current terms identify Aion Labs as a Deep Forge brand and limit rights in its served models to use through the service. They do not publish a downloadable Aion 2.0 weight license.

sources.title: AionLabs: Aion-2.0 | OpenRouter
sources.evidence: Reopened exact model page: current description matches the developer named DeepSeek V3.2 variant relation and supplies no parameter count. Its February 23, 2026 release date still conflicts with the developer December 21, 2025 date. The OpenRouter listing is corroborating provider metadata, not a separate Aion training report.

sources.title: Models.dev Aion-2.0 record
sources.evidence: Baseline source uses the generic reasoning-workflow description and false open_weights flag. Its comment cites the Aion API date as the release-date source; not independent technical verification.

sources.title: aionlabsai GitHub profile
sources.evidence: Reopened profile linked by official Hugging Face organization: zero public repositories. No Aion 2.0 implementation or configuration is published there.

sources.title: AionLabs: Aion-2.0 provider listing
sources.evidence: Provider catalog explicitly calls Aion-2.0 a fine-tuned variant of DeepSeek V3.2 from AionLabs. Used only to corroborate the interpretation of Aion Labs named-variant statement; it is not an independent first-party training or parameter disclosure.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Aion-2.0 endpoints API
sources.evidence: Fresh API response identifies one AionLabs endpoint, aion-labs/aion-2.0-20260223, and repeats the DeepSeek V3.2 variant description. No total/active parameter count, distillation, pruning or expert expansion is described; quantization is unknown.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 official model card
sources.evidence: Exact DeepSeek-V3.2 card metadata names deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-Base with base_model_relation finetune. The text explicitly states that V3.2 has the same model structure as V3.2-Exp. This provides the base-to-post-trained link for DeepSeek nominal specifications; it is not an Aion-specific tensor census.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V4 technical report, Table 1: DeepSeek-V3.2-Base specifications
sources.evidence: Later first-party Table 1 explicitly labels the DeepSeek-V3.2-Base column as MoE, 671B total parameters and 37B activated parameters. These are developer nominal main-model specifications, not counts of every serialized auxiliary MTP tensor. The exact V3.2 card and identical base/instruct configurations support using this nominal size for its post-trained model.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 official checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh read specifies DeepseekV32ForCausalLM, 61 main layers, first 3 dense, 256 routed experts, 8 selected per token, 1 shared expert and DSA indexer fields. Configuration bytes are identical to the named Exp-Base configuration, SHA-256 c7fa8b191e9936d8e6a57d864baab82b792fae16a116416cdd3a75ba76bc5af1. One next-token-prediction layer is configured, so nominal main-model scope must not be presented as an exact complete checkpoint count.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp-Base official checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Fresh configuration read is byte-identical to the final V3.2 configuration, including layer widths, expert count, routing top-k, DSA and MTP depth. The exact V3.2 card names this base and labels its relation as fine-tuning, corroborating unchanged structure across DeepSeek post-training.

sources.title: DeepSeek-V3.2 technical report, architecture and post-training
sources.evidence: Section 2 says V3.2 uses exactly the V3.2-Exp architecture; the only architectural change from V3.1-Terminus is DSA. Section 3 describes post-training the pre-trained V3.2 base into the final checkpoint. These establish the exact base-model relationship; no Aion-specific architectural statement is made.

sources.title: Official Aion Labs Hugging Face repository inventory
sources.evidence: Fresh public API lists only Aion-RP-Llama-3.1-8B and Aion-RP-Llama-3.1-8B-GGUF. No newer Aion 2.0 configuration or parameter disclosure was found in the official repository inventory.

name.note: Exact model ID confirmed. Developer display uses Aion 2.0; OpenRouter retains the catalog hyphenated spelling.

developer.note: Aion Labs publishes and serves this variant; underlying DeepSeek lineage should not be omitted from its family and description.

family.note: Explicitly described by the developer as a variant of DeepSeek V3.2.

release_date.note: Developer documentation and API agree. OpenRouter displays 2026-02-23; retain the original developer date rather than the conflicting provider date.

open_weights.note: Current official distribution is a hosted service; the official model organization exposes no Aion 2.0 download and the service terms grant only service-use rights. This does not claim an exhaustive search of every host.

license.note: No model-specific weight license published in inspected primary sources. API service terms are available, but the upstream model license must not be assigned to this variant automatically.

parameters_b.note: Nominal main-model size inferred from Aion Labs explicit DeepSeek V3.2 variant identity, corroborated by the provider fine-tune description. DeepSeek publishes 671B for V3.2-Base; the final V3.2 card names its base and its configuration is byte-identical. No pruning, smaller-model distillation, expert expansion or modality change was found in the inspected Aion sources. Aion does not independently publish a numeric total: this is a labeled lineage inference, not an exact complete Aion checkpoint or auxiliary-MTP count. The absence of a released Aion tensor census is not the reason for uncertainty.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal main-model active count inferred through the same explicit DeepSeek V3.2 lineage. DeepSeek Table 1 publishes 37B activated for V3.2-Base; matching base/final configurations preserve the 8-of-256 routed expert structure. Aion-specific routing modifications are not disclosed, so 37B is a qualified inherited nominal specification, not direct Aion attestation or an exact per-token/auxiliary-MTP accounting.

architecture.note: MoE inferred from the developer-named DeepSeek V3.2 variant and corroborating fine-tune description. The exact DeepSeek configuration has 256 routed experts with 8 selected per token and a shared expert, alongside MLA and DSA. No contrary Aion structural-change evidence was found; Aion has not released its own configuration.

context_window.note: Exact API context_length; documentation rounds it to 128K.

reasoning.note: Explicit capability flag and documented reasoning controls for Aion 2.0.

tool_call.note: Explicit tool_calls true flag; reference defines it as accepting tools and returning tool calls.

description.value: Aion Labs variant of DeepSeek V3.2 optimized for roleplay and storytelling, with reasoning and tool calling.
description.note: Replace generic workflow copy with the documented lineage and intended specialization; avoid unmeasured comparative performance claims.

patch.description: Aion Labs variant of DeepSeek V3.2 optimized for roleplay and storytelling, with reasoning and tool calling.
patch.notes: Nominal 671B main-model parameters, 37B active and MoE are inferred from Aion Labs explicit DeepSeek V3.2 variant lineage and DeepSeek specifications; Aion has not published separate counts or structural changes. These are inherited nominal specifications, not an exact complete checkpoint count. Developer release date: 2025-12-21; OpenRouter lists 2026-02-23.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit accepts 671B nominal main-model total, 37B nominal main-model active and MoE as explicitly labeled inferences from Aion Labs named DeepSeek V3.2 variant lineage. Reopened Aion docs/API, official HF inventory/GitHub and OpenRouter; searched for newer counts, fine-tuning and structural changes. Provider fine-tune wording corroborates lineage, while the first-party DeepSeek table and exact base/final configuration match establish the nominal specifications. No inspected Aion source identifies pruning, smaller-model distillation, expanded experts or a changed modality. Direct Aion-specific counts, exact implementation and auxiliary-MTP deployment remain undisclosed; do not substitute the base checkpoint storage aggregate or exact complete count. Preserve all unrelated audit fields and the release-date discrepancy.
